title: Olympic Basketball
text:
How did player ages differ across men’s basketball teams at the 2016 Olympics? I used TidyTuesday data from August 6, 2024 to compare the teams.
The full data cover the Olympics from 1896 to 2016. RGriffin put the Sports Reference records on Kaggle. I kept the men’s basketball event in 2016. This gives 141 players from 12 teams. Each player has one row and an age.
library(tidyverse)

olympics <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-08-06/olympics.csv')

basketball <- filter(olympics, sport == "Basketball", year == 2016, sex == "M")
Each box shows the middle half of a team’s ages. The line in the box marks the median.
ggplot(basketball, aes(x = age, y = team)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkorange") +
  labs(
    title = "Player ages by team",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Team"
  )
China has the lowest median age at 22.5 years. Brazil has the highest at 31. The United States falls between them at 26. Argentina has a wide age range, from 21 to 39.
The records list 10 players for Croatia and 11 for Nigeria. Each other team has 12. These comparisons use the players in the data.

title: Movie Budgets
text:
Do films with bigger budgets earn more at the box office? I used TidyTuesday data from October 23, 2018 to look at film budgets and ticket sales. The data come from The Numbers.
I removed one repeated row and kept films with box office totals above zero. This leaves 3,364 films from 1936 to 2018. The dollar amounts do not account for inflation.
library(tidyverse)

movies <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2018/2018-10-23/movie_profit.csv')

movies <- select(movies, movie, release_date, production_budget, worldwide_gross)
movies <- distinct(movies)
movies <- filter(movies, worldwide_gross > 0)
Each point shows one film. Both axes use millions of US dollars.
ggplot(movies, aes(x = production_budget / 1000000,
                  y = worldwide_gross / 1000000)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Movie budgets and box office revenue",
    x = "Production budget (US$ millions)",
    y = "Worldwide box office (US$ millions)"
  )
Films with bigger budgets tend to bring in more at the box office, but the points spread out. Films with close budgets can have very different ticket sales. Minions, for example, had a budget of $74 million and brought in about $1.16 billion worldwide.

title: Who gets mentioned in Suits?
text:
Which characters appear most often in Suits episode summaries, and how do mentions change by season?
The data contain 134 TVmaze episode summaries across nine seasons. Each character counts once per summary when their first name appears. These counts measure mentions in summaries, not screen time.

title: Who gets mentioned in Suits?
text:
Prepare the data

library(tidyverse)

suits <- read_csv("data/suits_episodes.csv")

suits <- suits |>
  mutate(
    text = str_replace_all(summary, "<[^>]+>", " "),
    text = str_to_lower(text),
    season = str_extract(url, "(?<=suits-)\\d+(?=x)")
  )


suits <- suits |>
  mutate(
    Harvey = str_detect(text, "\\bharvey\\b"),
    Mike = str_detect(text, "\\bmike\\b"),
    Louis = str_detect(text, "\\blouis\\b"),
    Donna = str_detect(text, "\\bdonna\\b"),
    Jessica = str_detect(text, "\\bjessica\\b"),
    Rachel = str_detect(text, "\\brachel\\b")
  )

mentions <- suits |>
  select(season, Harvey, Mike, Louis, Donna, Jessica, Rachel) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Harvey:Rachel,
    names_to = "character",
    values_to = "mentioned"
  )

title: Who gets mentioned in Suits?
text:
Which characters appear most often?

overall <- mentions |>
  group_by(character) |>
  summarise(episodes = sum(mentioned))

ggplot(overall, aes(x = episodes,
                    y = fct_reorder(character, episodes))) +
  geom_point(color = "navy", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Harvey appears in the most episode summaries",
    x = "Episode summaries mentioning the character (out of 134)",
    y = "Character"
  )








Harvey gets mentioned the most, showing up in 123 of the 134 summaries. Mike comes next with 96, then Louis with 86. Rachel has 50, Jessica has 45, and Donna has 39. Some characters are in the show for more seasons than others, so they have more chances to be mentioned.

title: Who gets mentioned in Suits?
section: How do mentions change by season?
text:
How do mentions change by season?

by_season <- mentions |>
  filter(character %in% c("Harvey", "Mike", "Louis")) |>
  group_by(season, character) |>
  summarise(
    episodes = n(),
    mentions = sum(mentioned),
    percent = 100 * mentions / episodes
  )

ggplot(by_season,
       aes(x = season, y = percent, color = character,
           group = character)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Character mentions change across seasons",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Episode summaries mentioning the character (%)",
    color = "Character"
  )








The seasons have different numbers of episodes, so this plot uses percentages. Harvey shows up in at least 80% of the summaries each season. The biggest change is Mike: he goes from being mentioned in every summary in season 7 to none in season 8, then two out of ten in season 9. Louis gets mentioned most often in seasons 6 and 7, appearing in 15 out of 16 summaries in each.
